narrative.overview:
RouterLM presents operational complexity through a calm, familiar macOS-inspired workspace. The interface is compact and information-dense, but its neutral canvas, restrained type scale, and carefully separated surfaces keep routing and provider health legible during production work.

The visual language uses light and dark tonal layers, floating glass navigation, crisp white panels, and small system-color signals for health. Motion is brief and functional: controls respond with subtle color or scale changes, and transient feedback rises in a small glass toast.
keyCharacteristics: Neutral light and dark themes with shared semantic roles.
Floating sidebar and top bar with blur reserved for chrome and transient feedback.
Compact data tables and metric bands with tabular numerals.
Green, amber, and red reserved for operational state.
The public client docs share every token and shape; only their reading ramp and page structure are their own (see Docs Surface).

rules.name: The State-Only Accent Rule
rules.body: Use green, amber, and red to communicate gateway state. Do not use them as decorative branding or arbitrary emphasis.

rules.name: The Numeric-Clarity Rule
rules.body: Apply tabular numerals to requests, latency, usage, percentages, and other values users compare vertically.

rules.name: The Reading-Size Rule
rules.body: Conversation text reads at 13px; data, controls and receipts stay at 12px, and meta at 11px. Code inside an answer drops back to 12px. Below 760px the composer input rises to 16px so mobile browsers don't zoom on focus.

rules.name: The Layered-Surface Rule
rules.body: Keep resting content surfaces flat and let tonal contrast, one-pixel separators, and soft ambient shadows establish hierarchy.

rules.name: The Ruled-Receipt Rule
rules.body: Under an answer, separate with a hairline, never a card; the answer stays the subject.

rules.name: The Token-Bridge Rule
rules.body: Vendored components inherit DESIGN.md tokens; they never bring their own palette, and shadcn's global `--primary` / `--muted` variables stay undefined because those names already mean something else here.

rules.name: The Reading-Measure Rule
rules.body: Prose, lede and lists read at `72ch`; only the title block, code figures and tables take the sheet's full width (the sheet is at most `980px`).

rules.name: The Literal-Mono Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono sets code figures, inline code and the title block's literal values (endpoint, page, revision); never labels, headings or prose.

rules.name: The Numbered Sheet Rule
rules.body: Sections carry page.section numbers and subsections page.section.subsection, set before the heading in faint tabular numerals (600; `0.6em` and `0.72em` of the heading); figures are captioned FIG. with the two-digit page and the figure count (FIG. 03-1). Every number comes from CSS counters reset per page, so they always match the contents.

rules.name: The Same-Theme, Own-Structure Rule
rules.body: Docs take every token and shape from this file and never the dashboard's shell. Dashboard pages never take the docs shell.

dos: Do preserve the neutral-first canvas and reserve semantic color for gateway state.
Do use Plus Jakarta Sans and tabular numerals for operational data.
Do keep panels in the `18px` radius family and controls in the `8–10px` family; use `6px`, `12px` and `14px` only for the jobs recorded in Shapes.
Do keep glass and blur limited to surfaces that float above content.
Do provide keyboard-visible focus and responsive mobile drawer behavior.
Do set conversation text at 13px and keep data, receipts and controls at 12px.
Do restyle vendored shadcn-vue and AI Elements components with Tailwind classes on their `class` prop.
donts: Don't introduce gradients, decorative patterns, or arbitrary bright accents.
Don't use pills for large buttons, cards, or navigation containers.
Don't turn every metric into a separate floating card; preserve the band and panel compositions.
Don't use monospace as a generic technical costume; reserve tabular numerals for measured data.
Don't use green, amber, or red for branding or emphasis unrelated to operational state.
Don't target vendored components with dashboard stylesheet rules, or define shadcn's colour variables globally.
Don't box a receipt or other answer footnote in a card; rule it off with a hairline.
